Literally thousands of colleges, libraries, and various public institutions were built thanks to them.

In my opinion dynastic wealth screws up capitalism. Our system worked (and works) incredibly well on a small scale when all the players are relatively close together. This in turn massively inflates companies somewhat arbitrarily which has a domino effect of rewarding things that aren't particularly meritorious in the market. The best way to make money in America today is not to create a good product, but to create a product that's attractive to these people who have vast sums of money but no personal merit or competence. How do you think things like Juicero were able to raise hundreds of millions? Or how Slack today is valued at billions of dollars?

I think it's a shame that today billionaires along the lines of Elon Musk are the exception. Not really the place for this conversation, but that's mostly just FUD spread by his competitors. These are the figures used by the LA Times in the hitpiece that largely started this. Conveniently, and surprisingly, they actually sourced their claims on his so-called subsidies.

It's very misleading. It includes things like $1.5 billion as a "30% subsidy for solar installations." Problem is exactly $0 of that goes to Musk or any of his companies. That's a consumer-only tax rebate. The exact same is true of the "federal income tax credits for buyers of Model S sedans." That's $7,500 per car for up to 200k sold. Except once again that doesn't go to Musk or any of his companies - that's exclusively a tax rebate for the consumer.

And what "Nevada tax incentives for Gigafactory" is talking about is what happened when Musk was deciding to build the Gigafactory. States tend to offer incentives for companies building major infrastructure in their city. This was the process of a competitive bidding process which Nevada won. They actually do get that $1.3 billion (finally) and in exchange Nevada gets thousands of new jobs and billions more in additional new tax revenue on top. I'll give you $30 to setup your company that'll give me $100 here. It's a similar situation for the New York solar panel factory. If you actually look at genuine subsidies that from taxpayers to Musk's companies, you're not going to find much of anything.

Now let's look at his competitors. $80 billion paid directly from the taxpayer to the massive auto industry in a bailout literally to stop failing companies from going out of business. In energy we give billions of dollars in real subsidies to the fossil fuel industry each year. In a report setup ahead of the G20 (where the US is coming under fire for continuing to subsidize fossil fuels so heavily) the government wrote up this report on the subsidies - totaling more than $8 billion a year and likely substantially lowballed the actual figures. In the space industry it's even more ridiculous Boeing/Locked receive literally $1 billion a year for doing absolutely nothing. It's a 'launch assurance subsidy' which basically means we want to make sure they stay in business even if they're not earning any money so the US government has a way to launch stuff - so they arbitrarily give them a billion bucks of taxpayer funds each and every year.

Maybe this is all an even bigger reflection of our society. We're not just failing to innovate but actually attacking it when it happens. Go launch a $600 juicer that serves little no purpose whatsoever (you could do an even easier/quicker job just squeezing the packets by hand) or a glorified instant messenger and you get media accolades, countless investors, and praise. Launch industries that are genuinely changing the world and revolutionizing industry as we know it, and you face a relentless assault from the established players in those industries that 99% of the time would be sufficient to destroy a company.

And while Musk does receive positive media when he's in the news, there's a desperate lack of it. For instance I was recently talking to a friend, an engineer who's also a space enthusiast, and he had literally no clue that just a couple of months SpaceX launched and landed 2 rockets on floating landing pads in the sea - all within 72 hours. Seriously, they had reusable rockets coming back on two different ships at the same time. Not only doing what people were saying was literally impossible, but doing it rapidly and accurately - completely ground breaking. It's amazing how much, and how rapidly, the world is changing. The news that weekend was instead rambling on about some Trump Russia conspiracy theory that turned out to be complete rubbish. Talk about priorities...
